essence: A one billion dollar market of solo founders pays in time, not money, to keep their venture story coherent as it changes.
plain_language: The market is founders who already pay for one productivity tool and feel the pain when documents contradict each other. They do not search for a fix, so the win comes from being in their feed and catching one named contradiction that would have cost them a round.
governing_thought: The wedge is solo second-time founders who feel the cost of an incoherent venture story, and the only channel that reaches them is founder-authored content plus peer recommendation.

mental_model.analogy: It is like selling umbrellas to people who do not yet know it is raining.
mental_model.mapping: The founders are the people. The rain is the silent contradictions already soaking their venture story. The umbrella is the tool. The trick is not the umbrella itself. It is standing next to them at the exact moment they feel their first drop and noticing they have nothing to hold over their head.
mental_model.limits: Unlike rain, venture contradictions never fully stop, so the umbrella has to stay open after the first use.

sweet_spot: The initial segment is narrow on purpose: second-time solo founders in their first twelve months, anchored on twenty dollar tools, converted by a live demo showing one cross-section cascade catch. Reach them through essays and peer posts, not paid ads. Expand only after a hundred of them share the same named win. The pond is big enough at one billion dollars, and a focused pitch wins it faster than a broad one.
key_claims: The working addressable market is about one point two billion dollars, growing twelve percent a year.
The wedge segment is second-time solo founders in the first twelve months of a new venture.
Incumbents store venture documents well but do not reason across them for contradictions.
Founders convert on a live demo that shows one cascade catch in the first minute, not on feature checklists.
Content and peer channels work; paid ads do not, because the pain has no keyword yet.
